SMTO-MEM-0015 — This file is bigger than Knowledge allows

GUID: 363b7ce4-6a5f-5a9a-9d10-a05792644b7e
Slug: knowledge-document-too-large
Domain: MEM · Subsystem: knowledge

What happened

  • The file is larger than the upload size limit set for Knowledge, so it wasn't added.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Split the file into smaller files, for example save each chapter or section as its own PDF or document. Each file is checked against the limit on its own, so smaller parts can be accepted.
  2. Upload the smaller files with Upload documents in Knowledge. Several parts in the same collection or conversation are searched together, just like one file.
  3. To allow bigger files, open Knowledge › Document settings, increase Maximum file size (bytes), and save. The limit is the smaller of this setting and the administrator's installation-wide limit.
  4. If it's still too big, ask the person who manages SMTO to raise Maximum upload size (bytes) under Administrator resource limits. Only an administrator can change the installation-wide ceiling.

What success looks like

  • The file appears in the document list and later shows Ready to search.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the file's size, to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete other sources to make room; this limit applies to each file, not to your total storage.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Knowledge rejected the upload because its size exceeds the smaller of the documents profile max_file_bytes and the installation max_file_bytes limit (64 MiB by default).

What this means

  • The selected file is larger than this installation permits for one upload. The original operation and completed work retain their own recorded outcomes; this diagnostic does not replay them.

Why this can happen

  • The component reported document_too_large. This does not establish the outcome of unrelated operations.

How to diagnose it

  • The smaller source is accepted for indexing.
  • Inspect the error reference and the affected component’s current observation before selecting a recovery action.

How to fix it

  • Compare the file size with max_file_bytes in Knowledge Document settings and max_file_bytes in the installation limits (Administrator resource limits; allowed range 1 KiB to 1 GiB). Raise whichever is lower, or split the source; nothing was stored for the rejected upload.
  • Split the file into smaller documents or ask an administrator to review Knowledge’s file limit before uploading again.

Retry and execution caution

  • The smaller source is accepted for indexing.

How to verify the fix

  • The smaller source is accepted for indexing.

What not to do

  • Do not delete retained task data or repeat an operation with an unknown outcome.

Technical notes

  • Status checks do not replay tasks or modify source documents.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
